title: Bound Qwen generation's machine footprint: per-job accelerator cache release, RSS-growth host recycle, RAM-scaled batch bounds, low synthesis priority
description: Follow-up to VieNeuTTSApp-mbzv (closed by the MAX_BATCH_CHARS cap). The batch char cap bounds ONE job, but a long export still ratchets the host's resident footprint: torch MPS/CUDA allocator caches are never released between jobs (_release_accelerator only runs on profile switch/fatal/shutdown), PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1 leaves CPU copies behind, and a host lives for hundreds of export jobs — so the 'largest process' OOM kill can still recur mid-chapter, and the parent never sees it coming. Batch bounds are also static (4 segments / 2000 chars), proven only on the 16 GB incident machine; an 8 GB machine can still OOM on a legal batch. Nothing lowers synthesis priority, so generation saturates CPU cores and lags the machine. Fix directions: (1) host releases accelerator cache after each settled job; (2) parent samples host RSS at job boundaries and recycles (clean shutdown + lazy respawn) when growth over the post-load baseline crosses a threshold (~1.5 GiB), before the kernel does it mid-job; (3) _segment_batches scales its segment/char bounds down for smaller physical RAM (>=16GiB full, >=8GiB 2/1024, below 1 segment); (4) host process drops CPU priority (nice / BELOW_NORMAL) and the in-process inference worker QThread runs at LowPriority.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for the bounds policy, the recycle-at-job-boundary behavior (fake footprint seam), the per-job cache release in the host frame loop, and the priority helpers; ruff clean; full unit suite passes.
notes: Implemented the resource governor for Qwen generation (bounds the PROCESS, complementing mbzv's per-JOB char cap). (1) Host: serve() releases the MPS/CUDA allocator caches after every settled job (_release_accelerator), so a long export's resident footprint tracks the working set instead of ratcheting; the host lowers its own CPU priority (os.nice(5) / BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS, logged as the 'priority' stderr event). (2) Parent: QwenEngine samples the host's RSS at job boundaries via an injectable footprint seam (ps on POSIX, GetProcessMemoryInfo on Windows) and recycles the host — clean shutdown + lazy respawn, baseline re-sampled post-load — when growth over the post-load baseline crosses RSS_RECYCLE_GROWTH_BYTES (1.5 GiB); growth-based so it self-calibrates per machine/dtype. (3) Batch bounds scale down with physical RAM (batch_bounds_for_ram: >=16GiB full 4/2000, >=8GiB 2/1024, below 1 segment x 512; protocol values stay the wire ceiling, unknown RAM keeps the ceiling); QwenEngineProvider derives them once per provider (explicit batch_bounds override wins). (4) In-process VieNeu path: InferenceWorker.run sets its QThread to LowPriority so CPU-device synthesis yields to the GUI. Tests: RAM-tier policy, shrink/clamp of _segment_batches, provider RAM-derived/cached/overridden bounds, recycle (triggered/kept/unknown-footprint/disabled/sampler-raises) + POSIX sampler sanity, per-job accelerator release over two sequential jobs, priority helpers + worker priority. Gates: 1806 unit + 19 non-slow smoke pass, ruff check+format clean. The one unit failure (test_app_entry single-instance) is pre-existing and environmental — reproduced on a stashed clean tree. Docs updated in docs/performance/qwen-runtime-compatibility.md (footprint-governor bullet). fp16/bf16-on-MPS remains the big lever and stays with no6w.

title: Qwen batch synthesis OOM-killed on 16GB Mac: cap batch memory + surface SIGKILL in host-closed error
description: macOS jetsam SIGKILLed the qwen host (python3.13 pid 87022, 22699 MB footprint) 25s into the new batch generate path: kernel log 2026-09-23 00:08:40 'memorystatus: killing largest compressed process python3.13 [87022] 22699 MB'. Parent saw only 'host closed its output stream (synthesizing)'. Factors: pinned mps float32 matrix (weights upcast ~2x), MAX_BATCH_SEGMENTS=4 x MAX_TEXT_CHARS=2000 in one generate_* call, MPS allocator caching, PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1 CPU fallback copies. Fix directions: cap batch segments/total chars per device RAM (or adapt MAX_BATCH_SEGMENTS), evaluate fp16/bf16 on MPS vs the pinned fp32 matrix, and make _read_frames include the child exit status (poll -> returncode -9 => 'killed by SIGKILL, likely memory pressure') in _publish_closed so this is self-diagnosing. Evidence: /usr/bin/log show window 2026-09-23 00:05-00:09.

(2) MAX_BATCH_CHARS (=MAX_TEXT_CHARS) in qwen_protocol caps the total text per synthesize_batch frame (validated in _validate_header_fields, enforced in QwenEngine.infer_stream_many), and QwenEngineProvider.infer_stream_segments splits batches greedily under both the segment and character bounds — a full-size segment still gets its own job. Batch generation now can never exceed the memory of the interactive single-segment worst case. (3) StudioTab regen/reset dialogs: the width moved off the contentItem Layout's implicitWidth onto the Dialog (the implicitWidth override re-entered the Basic style's implicitWidth binding — the reported loop at 354:5; the regen dialog at 236:5 had it too). Verified with an offscreen probe: 5 loop warnings pre-fix (354 and 236), 0 post-fix, dialogs still open and resize. Gates: 1790 unit + 19 non-slow smoke tests pass, ruff check+format clean. title: [bug] Windows CI: content_hash flakes on identical WAV bytes
description:
Latest CI run 35625626192: windows-x64 fails tests/unit/test_voice_profiles.py::test_the_content_hash_tracks_the_source_bytes (1 failed, 1729 passed). Linux green.

Root cause (verified locally): content_hash = sha256 of the raw source file bytes. libsndfile embeds a wall-clock timestamp in the PEAK chunk of every float WAV write, so two clips with identical audio written in different seconds differ at byte 60+ (proved: identical float32 buffers written ~2s apart are byte-different; audio samples decode identical).

Fix direction: hash the decoded/normalized audio payload (post-read mono float32 bytes + sample rate), not the container bytes. Keeps the dedup intent (same audio -> same clone) stable across writers/platforms.

title: [bug] Qwen synthesis fails for every language: the provider sends the model name where the host reads an app code
description:
User report: every Qwen CustomVoice job fails with 'Qwen3-TTS CustomVoice 0.6B does not support language 'English'/'Auto' — supported: auto, zh, en, ja, ko, de, fr, ru, pt, es, it' (four worker tracebacks, 'unexpected worker error').

Root cause: qwen_engine's provider mapped the app language code to the model's language name before sending the synthesize frame (language_model_name: 'en' -> 'English', 'auto' -> 'Auto'), but the host validates that field as an APP CODE (engine_profiles.validate_selection) and does the code -> name mapping itself before calling the model. So the host read a model name as an unknown code and refused every job. The buggy contract was pinned by three tests (engine provider x2, worker integration, e2e smoke), which is why it shipped: only the host test suite exercised the real host, and it sent codes.

Fix: the provider forwards the validated code; the host owns the mapping. Tests updated to pin the code on the wire.
acceptance_criteria: A Qwen job synthesizes for the profile default (auto) and for a picked language (en/zh); the synthesize frame carries the app code; the host still maps codes to model language names; the unsupported-language refusal still happens app-side before IPC.
notes:
Root cause: the provider pre-mapped the language (language_model_name) while the host validates app codes and maps them itself; every Qwen job died with 'does not support language 'English'' / 'Auto'.

Fix: qwen_engine._language now validates the code and forwards it unchanged; the host keeps owning code -> model-name mapping. Pinned by updated tests: engine provider x2 (frame carries 'zh'/'auto'), worker integration (frame 'zh'), e2e smoke (custom + base frames 'zh').

Verification: real host + fake model accepts 'auto'/'en'/'zh' and maps them to 'Auto'/'English'/'Chinese' (was: refused); the updated tests fail on the pre-fix provider (3 failures); 1734 unit+smoke tests pass; ruff check/format clean.

title: [bug] Managed Qwen runtime install spins for hours: quadratic wheel-conflict scan and misleading download size
description:
Installing the managed Qwen runtime (linux-x64-cpu, 87 wheels, 410 MB) never reaches ready. Evidence from a live session (~/.local/share/VieNeuTTSApp/qwen/runtime/.staging/qwen-runtime-v1): all 87 wheels downloaded, extraction stuck at wheel 40/87 with one pool thread pinned at ~100% CPU for 10+ minutes (553 s CPU) and no new files.

Root cause: managed_install.validate_wheel_layout's cross-archive conflict check scans every already-claimed output for every member, so validating the pinned closure is O(members x claimed_outputs) = ~431M Path comparisons (torch alone: 252M). Measured 92 ms per member against the real tree.

Second defect (what the Settings card shows): the card pairs 'Downloaded 410 MB of 820 MB' with an EMPTY progress bar. required_bytes comes from the installer's disk-space preflight (2x payload), not the download size, and the start-state publish of a resumed install leaves progress at 0.0 while reporting 410 MB already verified on disk.
acceptance_criteria: validate_wheel_layout keeps every unsafe-layout rejection (exact-path, file-under-directory in both orders) with O(members) work; a 2k+2k member closure validates in seconds; the runtime card's size denominator is the pinned payload and a resumed install reports progress consistent with the bytes on disk.
notes:
Root cause: managed_install.validate_wheel_layout compared every member against every already-claimed path — 431M Path comparisons for the pinned linux-x64-cpu closure (87 wheels / 29,375 members). Measured: 118.0s for a synthetic 3,000-member pair; a live session sat at wheel 40/87 with 553s of CPU and no new files.

Fix (managed_install.py): a claimed file now records its ancestors as implied directory claims, so 'something is already claimed below this path' is an O(1) dict hit. Every unsafe-layout rejection is preserved (exact path, file-under-directory in both orders, cross-wheel repeat) and pinned by new tests.

Fix (controller.py): the card reported status.required_bytes — the installer's 2x disk-space preflight — as the download size ('Downloaded 410 MB of 820 MB'), and a resumed install published progress 0.0 next to the bytes already verified. qwenRuntimeRequiredBytes now returns the pinned payload and the start/cancel/import publishes derive progress from installed/required.

Verification: real closure validates in 4.9s; install_from_offline_pack of the real 87 wheels reaches ready in 15.2s (30,542 files, re-inspect ready); new tests fail on the old code (118.0s vs <1s linearity); 1732 unit+smoke tests pass (only the pre-existing single-instance-lock failure, which passes with an isolated HOME); ruff check/format clean.

title: [bug] Engine backend resolved before NVIDIA driver probe lands — session stays on CPU despite ready managed CUDA
description:
Startup race: run_gui schedules refreshCudaRuntimeState at 130ms (probes nvidia-smi in bg, up to 3s timeout) but prewarm_engine at 500ms builds the engine via resolve_model_source(), which reads cudaRuntimeDriverReady — still False if nvidia-smi hasn't returned. The engine is then constructed with backend=onnx and persists for the whole session (_ensure_worker only builds once; _publish_cuda_runtime_driver_probe only resets _torch_available, never re-resolves the engine).

Result: a user with the managed runtime installed AND a working driver runs CPU ONNX for every launch where nvidia-smi takes >~370ms — common on Optimus/Advanced-Optimus laptops where the dGPU is powered down (nvidia-smi routinely takes 1-3s to wake it). Worse, the Settings engine note then flips to 'PyTorch · CUDA x.y' after the probe lands while the actual engine stays ONNX — the exact readout/backend disagreement managed_cuda_for_detection() was designed to prevent (controller.py ~1130).

Files: app.py:389-416 (timer ordering), controller.py:1155-1194 (probe flow), controller.py:3414-3445 (_ensure_worker), controller.py:1838-1855 (prewarm_engine), engine.py:189-217 (resolve_model_source).

Fix direction: don't resolve backend until the first driver probe lands (gate _ensure_worker/prewarm on _cuda_runtime_driver_checked when a managed runtime is installed, with a bounded wait), or re-resolve + rebuild the engine when the probe lands ready while the built engine is still uninitialized (is_initialized False).
close_reason: Fixed: AppController defers the 'auto' backend while the driver probe is in flight; TTSEngine._resolve_auto_backend waits (bounded 12 s) on managed_cuda_engine_state, so a slow nvidia-smi no longer pins the session to ONNX and the engine cannot disagree with the Settings readout. Tests: test_engine deferred-resolution suite + test_controller deferral tests.

title: [bug] Settings tab crashes with OverflowError on first visit (32-bit Qt int byte counts)
description:
Opening the Settings tab for the first time raised OverflowError and showed the fatal-error dialog; closing the app then spammed ~190 "Cannot read property X of null" QML TypeErrors on the terminal.

ROOT CAUSE (1): AppController exposed 4 byte counts as Qt `int` (32-bit): modelInstalledBytes, modelRequiredBytes, cudaRuntimeInstalledBytes, cudaRuntimeRequiredBytes. The linux-x64 managed CUDA manifest requires 2 x 3,961,706,230 = 7,923,412,460 bytes, so the meta-object read from SettingsTab.qml:419 (cudaRuntimeStorageLabel) raised OverflowError inside the QML binding; the exception unwound out of ShellBridge.setCurrentTab -> currentTabChanged.emit() into the crash handler.

ROOT CAUSE (2): run_gui had no deterministic QML teardown. At interpreter shutdown `engine` (which anchors bridge/controller/playback) is cleared before the QML tree, so bindings re-evaluate against null context properties: 186-192 TypeErrors in 5 of 6 measured close runs.

FIX: widen all four properties to `qlonglong`; add app._teardown_qml so run_gui destroys the QML tree while create_app anchors are alive (6 of 6 close runs silent).

VERIFICATION: repro driver with the real controller/manifest reproduced both defects pre-fix; new tests (tests/unit/test_controller.py::TestQmlByteProperties) fail pre-fix (OverflowError / truncated -666522132) and pass post-fix; 846 unit+integration tests and both offscreen QML smoke suites pass.

title: qwen_gguf_engine_20260923: Qwen 0.6B GGUF engine support
description:
# Qwen 0.6B GGUF engine support

## Overview

Add Serveurperso's GGUF conversions of Qwen3-TTS 12Hz 0.6B Base and
CustomVoice through an isolated, app-managed `qwentts.cpp` runtime. Users
choose the model profile first, then its format, an optional GGUF
quantization, the compatible engine, and a supported compute device.

The existing official-weight PyTorch path remains available and unchanged.
This track adds a second implementation of the same Qwen model profiles,
not four more top-level engine profiles.

**Approved decisions (2026-09-23):**

- Target CPU, NVIDIA CUDA, and Apple Metal. Exclude Vulkan.
- Label the existing option **Official full weights**, not FP16.
  Preserve `host_precision`: CPU/MPS FP32 and CUDA BF16.
- Offer **GGUF Q8_0** and **GGUF Q4_K_M** for both 0.6B profiles.
- Use an isolated managed host, not native inference in the GUI process.
- Execute the implementation plan sequentially.
- No per-phase manual verification or approval gates. Use automated task
  gates and final scripted real-model release checks.
- Medium priority; no prerequisite track; no time estimate.

## Current integration points

- `core/engine_profiles.py` defines the existing semantic profiles,
  languages, nine CustomVoice speakers, and Base enrollment requirements.
- `core/synthesis_context.py` carries immutable job/cache/Studio identity.
- `core/qwen_engine.py`, `core/qwen_protocol.py`, and
  `workers/qwen_host.py` implement the isolated official-weight path.
- `core/qwen_runtime.py`, `core/qwen_model_manager.py`, and
  `core/managed_install.py` provide verified install patterns.
- `ui/controller.py`, `EngineState.qml`, and `EngineProfilePicker.qml`
  provide global selection and readiness across synthesis surfaces.
- `core/voice_profiles.py` already persists source audio, transcript, and
  consent rather than opaque engine objects.

## Functional requirements

### FR-1: Model-first selection

1. Preserve the existing IDs `vieneu`, `qwen_base_0_6b`, and
   `qwen_custom_0_6b`.
2. For either Qwen profile, offer **Official full weights** and **GGUF**.
3. GGUF exposes exactly `Q8_0` and `Q4_K_M`. Default to `Q8_0` the first
   time GGUF is selected; remember the user's subsequent selection.
4. Show a compatible-engine selector/readout: official weights resolve to
   **PyTorch**, GGUF resolves to **qwentts.cpp**. With only one compatible
   engine, show it as the selected, non-editable choice. Never permit
   PyTorch+GGUF or qwentts.cpp+official weights.
5. Device choices depend on the engine, platform, installed runtime, and
   hardware. Display **Metal** for the native backend, not PyTorch's
   **MPS**. Auto chooses only a validated available device in the selected
   format; it never changes profile, format, or quantization.
6. Preserve current official-weight precision and device behavior. Display
   actual precision where diagnostics expose it; do not promise FP16.
7. Refuse selection changes while synthesis is running, queued, or
   cancelling. Async checks/install completions cannot publish readiness
   for an obsolete selection. An install targets the variant captured
   when it began, not whichever option is selected when it finishes.
8. Migrate old Qwen settings to official weights without changing voices,
   devices, or unrelated preferences. Fresh installs still default to
   VieNeu. Persist format, GGUF quantization, and separate engine-device
   preferences; corrupt new fields clamp individually.

### FR-2: Model and runtime installation

1. Support these talkers from `Serveurperso/Qwen3-TTS-GGUF`:
   - `qwen-talker-0.6b-base-Q8_0.gguf`
   - `qwen-talker-0.6b-base-Q4_K_M.gguf`
   - `qwen-talker-0.6b-customvoice-Q8_0.gguf`
   - `qwen-talker-0.6b-customvoice-Q4_K_M.gguf`
2. Pair each talker with the same-quantization
   `qwen-tokenizer-12hz-{Q8_0|Q4_K_M}.gguf`. Do not expose mixed talker/codec
   quantization in this track. Share a tokenizer across Base/CustomVoice
   only when revision, size, and digest identify the same file.
3. Pin the repository revision, exact filenames, byte sizes, SHA-256
   digests, and compatible native runtime build. Never install from a
   moving `main`/`HEAD` URL at runtime.
4. Distribute verified native library/backend packs separately from models
   and the frozen application. Install/download, cancel, retry, repair,
   remove, inspect storage, and import a matching offline pack.
5. Reuse staging, resume, free-space checks, verification, atomic promotion,
   rollback, Windows path/lock handling, and in-use removal guards.
   Reject traversal, escaping links, incompatible pack identities, and
   incomplete or corrupt packs before readiness becomes true.
6. Keep official and GGUF installs independently usable. Removing one
   variant cannot remove another variant's files, a referenced shared
   tokenizer, or enrolled clone recordings.
7. GGUF requires no PyTorch runtime, pip invocation, user compiler, Docker,
   arbitrary executable path, or manually discovered Python environment.
   Maintainers build packs; the application only installs verified packs.

### FR-3: Isolated native inference

1. Use a thin app-owned host process binding the pinned qwentts.cpp C ABI.
   In source mode it uses the app interpreter; frozen builds re-dispatch
   the application through `--qwen-gguf-host`. Native libraries load only
   in that child, from the verified runtime directory.
2. Reuse the framed, bounded, job-tagged IPC contract and parent lifecycle
   discipline. Negotiate native capabilities explicitly; do not pretend
   Metal is a PyTorch MPS device or advertise native batch support without
   evidence. Unsupported protocol/build combinations fail actionably.
3. Preserve exactly one resident model owner across VieNeu, official Qwen,
   and GGUF. Reuse a loaded native context across bounded segments rather
   than starting a CLI/model load for every segment.
4. Feed real native audio callbacks through a stateful, per-segment
   24 kHz-to-48 kHz mono float32 resampler into the existing artifact-first
   writer and bounded preview transport. Do not buffer the whole document.
   Keep native logs off the IPC stdout channel.
5. Keep the GUI cancellation path nonblocking. Cancel-before-pickup,
   cancellation during load/inference, late audio, host crash, and shutdown
   settle each admitted job once. Escalate cancel to terminate/kill/reap
   outside the GUI thread when the native API cannot stop promptly.
6. After cancellation or crash, the next job may lazily restart a clean
   host. Never complete or autoplay a cancelled generation.
7. Bound CPU threads, queued output, segment sizes, and reference caches;
   retain the existing job-boundary footprint-governor behavior where
   applicable without imposing PyTorch-specific knobs on GGML.
8. Explicit unsupported devices, OOM, missing native dependencies, bad
   model metadata, and ABI mismatch produce recovery guidance. No silent
   cross-format fallback, hidden model download, or runtime network access.

### FR-4: Voices and capability mapping

1. Base remains the clone profile: reference audio, matching transcript,
   and consent are required, including for GGUF.
2. CustomVoice remains the fixed-speaker profile. Map existing speaker IDs
   to native IDs explicitly, including casing (`Uncle_Fu` → `uncle_fu`).
3. Preserve the existing ten Qwen languages plus Auto as the intended
   capability set. Verify each mapping against the pinned native runtime.
   An unsupported mapping is rejected with a reason, never guessed.
   Do not add languages based solely on the current upstream README.
4. Do not add instruction/style controls for the 0.6B variants.
5. Reuse Base enrollment source recordings/transcripts across formats.
   Normalize native reference input to the ABI's required mono 24 kHz.
   Rebuild engine-specific prompts/latents; never pass PyTorch objects to
   the native runtime. Any derived cache includes source-content hash,
   transcript, model/tokenizer identity, quantization, and native build.
6. Verify Base/CustomVoice semantics against native code and real-model
   output before enabling them. The model card's mode table conflicts
   with the runtime README; filenames alone are not compatibility evidence.

### FR-5: Provenance and all synthesis surfaces

1. Snapshot profile, format, quantization, engine/runtime build identity,
   pinned model/tokenizer identity, resolved device, language, voice/clone,
   and generation settings when admitting a job.
2. Carry that identity into artifacts, audiobook/subtitle cache keys,
   batch jobs, and Studio clips. Different format/quantization/runtime
   identities cannot share a cached render.
3. Migrate old known Qwen provenance as official-weight provenance, never
   as GGUF. Unknown new schemas become cache misses; wholly unstamped
   legacy renders retain the existing VieNeu-only compatibility rule.
4. Studio displays the recorded model/engine/quantization, guards
   re-synthesis against a variant mismatch, and offers an explicit switch
   to the recorded selection. Unavailable recorded revisions/builds are
   explained, not silently replaced.
5. Cover Text, Paragraph, multi-file Batch, Audiobook, Subtitle, Audio
   Studio, voice audition, playback, and WAV/MP3 export. Native batch
   operations may serialize bounded segments in one resident host.
6. Keep selection/readiness in one Python contract and the shared
   `EngineState` derivation. Add reusable QML controls, not per-tab copies.
   Retain existing objectName contracts and Vietnamese/English localization.

## Non-functional requirements

- **Platform target:** Windows x64 CPU/CUDA, Linux x64 CPU/CUDA, and
  macOS Apple Silicon CPU/Metal, six matrix cells. Do not claim support
  until the corresponding native pack and real-model evidence pass.
- **Release gate:** both profiles × both quantizations × all six cells,
  24 primary synthesis combinations, plus lifecycle and offline checks.
  Missing release hardware remains an explicit blocker, not a passed test.
- **Security/privacy:** no inference listener port, shell-built commands,
  unverified native library discovery, user-text logging, or reference-audio
  telemetry. Native code is third-party code and must remain pinned and
  isolated. Preserve MIT/Apache-2.0 notices in redistributed packs.
- **Startup/dependencies:** no model load/native ABI import on GUI startup;
  no Qwen PyTorch stack or native model weights added to `pyproject.toml`,
  `uv.lock`, or the frozen base bundle.
- **Performance:** measure load time, first audio, real-time factor,
  current/peak RSS, and GPU memory where available. Do not copy upstream
  leaderboard claims into app guarantees. Preserve responsive cancellation,
  bounded preview transport, and single-owner operation.
- **Testing:** ordinary CI uses deterministic fake hosts and tiny
  installation fixtures, with no real weights or network. Real-model
  checks are explicit, opt-in, and use the application's own install/host
  path. Target at least 80% line coverage on changed Python logic.
  No phase requires manual user verification or approval to proceed.
- **UI:** responsive down to the existing 640×420 minimum; truthful active
  variant, storage, runtime readiness, device, and error states.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC-1:** Both Qwen profiles offer official weights, GGUF Q8_0, and GGUF
  Q4_K_M; only compatible engines/devices can be selected.
- **AC-2:** Old settings preserve the official path and device precision;
  new settings round-trip without resetting unrelated preferences.
- **AC-3:** All four talkers and two shared tokenizers have pinned manifests,
  correct pairing, independent lifecycle, and verified offline installs.
- **AC-4:** Native runtime packs install/repair/remove safely without
  PyTorch, compilers, arbitrary executable discovery, or GUI-thread loads.
- **AC-5:** Base cloning and all nine CustomVoice speakers work for both
  quantizations with validated language/Auto mappings.
- **AC-6:** Real native streaming reaches 48 kHz artifacts and bounded
  preview correctly; segment boundaries do not reset resampler state
  within a segment or lose its final samples.
- **AC-7:** Cancellation, crashes, switching, and shutdown leave no
  overlapping model owners, stale audio, blocked GUI, or orphan host.
- **AC-8:** Variant-aware provenance prevents cross-format/quantization
  cache reuse and makes Studio restoration/re-synthesis explicit.
- **AC-9:** Existing Base clones work across formats from their stored
  source data; derived data never crosses incompatible runtimes.
- **AC-10:** All synthesis surfaces and localized UI pass consolidated
  fake-host scenarios; VieNeu and official Qwen behavior does not regress.
- **AC-11:** Frozen source/packaging paths locate the pinned native host
  assets correctly and classify missing native dependencies actionably.
- **AC-12:** The 24-combination real-model matrix, resource/cancel/offline
  checks, license inventory, documentation, and repository quality gates
  pass before advertising the complete target matrix as supported.

quantization, GGUF F32/BF16, new FP16 precision controls, local model

title: Cancel on Text tab freezes the GUI while a Qwen generation settles
description: User report: on the Text tab, clicking Generate then Cancel for a long text with the Qwen engine shows 'Canceling' but nothing happens. Root cause 1: StudioController.cancel() runs worker.cancel_job() on the GUI thread; the worker's _signal_active_cancel calls provider.cancel() synchronously, and QwenEngine.cancel blocks in _wait_cancelled until the host's uninterruptible generate call returns (heartbeats prove liveness; escalation waits up to cancel_grace_timeout=300s). The whole window freezes. Root cause 2: QwenEngine._run_job sends the synthesize frame before checking the remembered cancel request, so a cancel that lands during the lazy model load or between batches still burns a full generate pass before settling.
acceptance_criteria: 1) cancel_job/cancel_owner return promptly; the provider cancel runs on a background thread (GUI stays responsive; spec: 'Main thread never blocks'). 2) A pre-start cancel (before the synthesize frame is sent, including during a lazy load) refuses the job without sending any frame to the host. 3) A mid-generation cancel still settles cooperatively when the host's generate returns (existing engine cancel semantics and tests preserved; stop() teardown stays synchronous). 4) Unit tests cover both fixes; existing suites pass.
notes: Fixed both defects. (1) workers/inference_worker.py _signal_active_cancel now dispatches _cancel_provider_job on a daemon thread, so cancel_job/cancel_owner return immediately and the GUI thread never waits for the Qwen host to settle (QwenEngine.cancel can block up to cancel_grace_timeout=300s while the uninterruptible generate runs). stop() stays synchronous on purpose: teardown must reap the host before exit. (2) core/qwen_engine.py _run_job refuses a job whose cancel arrived before its frame was sent — checked before the lazy load and again after it — via new _refuse_cancelled_job, so a pre-start cancel no longer burns a full autoregressive pass (previously the synthesize frame was sent first and the cancel only settled when generate returned). Tests: test_cancel_job_does_not_block_the_calling_thread (regression, failed 10.0s block before the fix), engine cold-load + pre-start refusal tests with a new slow_load fake-host mode, two release-smoke tests moved from a racy 10ms cancel to a deterministic 1000ms mid-job cancel. Full unit suite: 1827 passed, 1 pre-existing headless-audio env failure (test_real_qaudiosink_offscreen_smoke, fails identically on pristine tree).

[bug] Transient nvidia-smi probe failure is a dead end: no in-session driver re-check
description:
refreshCudaRuntimeState() runs exactly once at startup (app.py:400). If probe_cuda_driver() times out (3s) or fails once — sleeping dGPU wake, EDR/AV blocking the subprocess spawn, first-boot driver init — then cudaRuntimeDriverReady stays False, so cudaRuntimeInstallAllowed=False and the install button stays disabled.

installCudaRuntime() would re-probe when driver_checked is False (controller.py:1233-1263), but the button that triggers it is disabled precisely when the check failed; and once driver_checked=True+failed, that path early-returns anyway (controller.py:1265). SettingsTab.qml's driver guide offers only a download link — no 're-check' action. Only recovery: restart the app.

Fix direction: expose a re-check action in the driver-notice/guide area that calls refreshCudaRuntimeState() (it already re-probes the driver every run), and/or retry the probe automatically a few times with backoff before declaring the driver absent.
close_reason: Fixed: Settings CUDA card gained a 'Re-check driver' button (cudaRuntimeDriverRecheckButton) wired to refreshCudaRuntimeState(), which always re-runs inspect+probe; NVML-first detection also removes the transient subprocess failure mode. Smoke coverage added.

title: Expose TrimOp: region select on the master waveform (trim to / delete selection)
description:
core/studio.py already models TrimOp(start_frame, end_frame) and controller.studioPushTrim(start, end) (controller.py:2385) is a public slot - but no QML ever calls it (grep studioPushTrim in src/vienetts_app/ui/qml -> 0 hits). The master deck already supports click/drag seeking (PlaybackWaveform.seekable, StudioTab.qml:620), so the interaction surface exists. title: Studio clip list nests a 480 px ScrollView inside the page scroll (wheel trap)
description:
StudioTab.qml:1218 wraps the clip list in its own ScrollView with implicitHeight: Math.min(480, clipList.implicitHeight). With 20 clips (a 20-paragraph document, which the paragraph studio produces routinely) the inner content is 1272 px in a 480 px box, nested inside the page ScrollView (viewport 652, content 1562) - measured 2026-09-15.

This is another instance of the known hazard recorded in beads memory qml-scroll-perf-bench: 'nested flickables consume wheel events before the page scroll - two-phase handoff feels jumpy'. The inner bar does render (measured: visible, size 0.377), so the list is scrollable - but the wheel over the list scrolls the list, not the page, and the list is capped at 480 px inside a page that already scrolls 1562 px. Two nested scroll regions for one list is one too many, and the cap makes the page taller than it needs to be.

Fix direction: drop the inner ScrollView and let the page scroll own the list (the page already scrolls), or keep a capped list with an explicit 'show all N segments' affordance. Acceptance: one wheel gesture over the clip list scrolls the page; no hidden overflow.

title: Studio: Apply is silent while Undo/Reset auto-play, and every op kills playback (no A/B)
description:
_push_studio_op (controller.py:2288) calls _emit_studio(kind=kind) with auto_preview defaulting to False, so an Apply changes the audio silently. studioUndo (controller.py:2412) and studioReset (controller.py:2427) pass auto_preview=True and start playback. The user therefore hears the change they undid but never the change they made.

Separately, every mutating action calls _invalidate_studio_preview() (controller.py:2224, called at 2303/2402/2422/2436/2455/2654), which stops playback and zeroes replayDurationMs, so the playhead and the timecode reset to 0:00 on every tweak. Auditioning a chain of ops means: scroll up, press Nghe thu, scroll down, apply, scroll up, press Nghe thu...

Design question to settle (needs a product decision): does Apply audition automatically, or is there an explicit 'Apply and audition' / continuous-audition toggle? Recommended: keep Apply silent (long mixes re-render), but (1) keep the playhead/position instead of resetting to 0, (2) make undo/apply consistent, and (3) add a persistent 'Nghe thu' affordance that does not scroll away (see the layout issue). Acceptance: applying an op leaves the transport in a predictable, documented state; Apply and Undo behave consistently.

title: Studio rack readouts misstate the rendered mix (ops accumulate, sliders show the last one)
description:
GainOp/SpeedOp/FadeOp/NormalizeOp/SilenceTrimOp are appended to the op tuple and every one of them is applied by render_project (core/studio.py:118), so repeated Apply compounds. But controller.studioControls (controller.py:2060) returns the value of the LAST op of each kind and StudioTab.syncControls (StudioTab.qml:82) pushes that into the sliders. The rack therefore labels the mix wrongly.

Measured (2026-09-15, core/studio.py directly):
  gain: dry peak 0.2000 -> one +3 dB Apply 0.2825 (+3.0 dB) -> two Applies 0.3991 (+6.0 dB). Rack still reads 'Gain: 3.0 dB'.
  speed: dry 48000 frames -> one 1.15x 41739 (0.870x) -> two 1.15x 36295 (1.322x total). Rack still reads 'Speed: 1.15x'.
  gap: GapOp is last-wins (render_project pre-scans and keeps the last GapOp), so its label happens to be right while both ops stay in the history.

Two acceptable fixes, pick one deliberately:
  (a) parameter semantics: Apply replaces the previous op of the same kind in place (keep the stack as a parameter set), or
  (b) display semantics: expose the EFFECTIVE controls (cumulative gain, cumulative speed, effective gap) as the slider values, and let the history show every step.
Either way 'Hoan tac' must keep working and the displayed value must equal what render_project produces. Acceptance: a test asserts slider value == measured effect for 2x gain, 2x speed, and a gap change.

title: Per-clip preview reuses the master transport: labels show the clip, waveform shows the whole mix
description:
studioPreviewClip (controller.py:2488) sets replayDurationMs to the CLIP length and drives replayPosition from the clip's playback, but studioEnvelope keeps the whole-mix envelope and StudioTab binds the master waveform to durationMs = replayDurationMs (StudioTab.qml:626). Result: while auditioning clip #3 the master waveform sweeps its full-mix envelope in clip time, and the timecode reads e.g. '0:01 / 0:02' for a 10 s project. There is also no per-clip playing state, so no row shows which clip is sounding; the row's play button stays a plain play icon.

Fix direction: either give the clip audition its own transport/position property (clipPlayingId + clipPosition) and dim the master deck, or render the clip's own envelope into the deck and label it as a clip preview. Acceptance: while a clip previews, the highlighted row, the timecode, and the waveform all describe the same audio.

title: Source-install CUDA path is non-functional: engine requires the managed runtime, README/benchmarks say otherwise
description:

So a source install with cu128 torch in the venv (README 'CUDA from source' section, lines ~164-173) still cannot run the torch backend in the app.

Same for the benchmark harnesses: scripts/benchmarks/run_engine.py and run_once.py construct TTSEngine(backend='torch') with no cuda_runtime -> initialize() raises.

1. Docs-only: rewrite the README source-CUDA section to say the app's CUDA engine always uses the managed runtime (install it from Settings even in source installs), and that the cu128 venv install only feeds diagnostics/benchmarks-that-support-it.
2. Code: let source installs use a system torch when no managed runtime is present (contradicts the 2026-09-06 managed-runtime design, which is managed-only by design) — needs a product decision.
3. Make benchmarks accept a --cuda-runtime path (or a --managed-runtime flag) so maintainers can benchmark torch without the GUI install flow.

title: Harden NVIDIA driver detection: NVML/ctypes path, longer timeout, nvidia-smi fallbacks
description:
probe_cuda_driver() (detector.py:87-111) has exactly one detection path: spawn 'nvidia-smi' with a 3s timeout. Failure modes that leave a working driver unrecognized:

- dGPU asleep (Optimus/d3cold): first nvidia-smi can take >3s → TimeoutExpired → unavailable.
- nvidia-smi.exe absent: NVCleanstall/stripped driver installs, minimal/Server setups. CreateProcess finds it in System32 for standard installs, but it is not guaranteed.
- EDR/AV blocking or delaying the subprocess spawn.

Suggested hardening, in order:
1. Try NVML directly via ctypes first — nvml.dll ships inside C:\Windows\System32 with every NVIDIA driver (libnvidia-ml.so.1 on Linux): nvmlInit_v2 + nvmlSystemGetCudaDriverVersion_v2 gives the same CUDA-version answer with no subprocess, no PATH dependence, no console window, and no spawn latency. torch itself uses NVML.
2. Fall back to nvidia-smi at the standard paths (System32 via default search; %ProgramFiles%\NVIDIA Corporation\NVSMI\nvidia-smi.exe).
3. Raise/relax the subprocess timeout (e.g., 8-10s) — this probe already runs off the GUI thread.
close_reason: Fixed: probe_cuda_driver() tries NVML via ctypes first (nvml.dll / libnvidia-ml.so.1), falls back to nvidia-smi on PATH and %PROGRAMFILES%\NVIDIA Corporation\NVSMI\nvidia-smi.exe, uses an 8 s timeout, CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows, and maps every failure to 'unavailable' instead of raising.

title: [bug] Driver gate requires reported CUDA >= 12.8 (R570+); cu128 wheels run on R528+/CUDA 12.0+ via minor-version compat
description:
probe_cuda_driver() gates on nvidia-smi's reported 'CUDA Version' >= 12.8 (detector.py REQUIRED_CUDA=(12,8); CudaDriverProbe.usable). That field is the driver's MAX supported CUDA — requiring 12.8 means requiring an R570+ driver.

But CUDA 12.x has minor-version compatibility: apps built against CUDA 12.x (and bundling their own cudart, as the managed cu128 wheels do) run on any driver >= R528.33 Windows / R525.60.13 Linux — i.e., drivers reporting 'CUDA Version: 12.0' through '12.7' would very likely run the managed torch cu128 fine. Those users are currently blocked from installing the runtime entirely.

Verify against torch 2.8.0+cu128's actual minimum driver before changing; if confirmed, gate on driver version (R528.33+) or reported CUDA >= 12.0 instead.
close_reason: Fixed: REQUIRED_CUDA=(12,0) after verifying cu128 minor-version compatibility (R525.60.13 Linux / R527.41 Windows); docs updated in README, PROJECT_PLAN.md, conductor/tech-stack.md and Settings driver guidance.

title: test_real_qaudiosink_offscreen_smoke fails on device-less hosts: local skip guard misses 'sink constructs without draining'
description:
Found at the 2026-09-16 conductor refresh.

tests/unit/test_stream_playback.py::TestRealQtSmoke::test_real_qaudiosink_offscreen_smoke fails with 'assert 19200 == 0' (bytesAvailable) on this Linux workstation. It is NOT a code regression and NOT purely flaky:

- Passes in isolation: single file at -n auto, at -n 14, and alone.
- Fails whenever it shares a run with >=2 unit files, SERIALLY too (-n 0), and with stream_playback listed first.
- Guarded by @pytest.mark.skipif(os.environ.get('CI') == 'true'), so CI is unaffected.

Root cause: the LOCAL skip guard only skips when controller.start() raises or controller.errorText is set. On a device-less host the ffmpeg backend constructs the sink 'successfully' (QtWarningMsg: No audio device detected) but never drains, so the drained-buffer assert fires instead of skipping. patterns.md line 136 already documents this CI-runner constraint ('guard on a CI env marker'); the local path was left uncovered.

Suggested fix: after controller.feed(...), treat a non-draining sink as environment-dependent — skip when no output device is present (e.g. QMediaDevices.defaultAudioOutput().isNull()) or when bytesAvailable() does not reach 0 within a short bounded pump loop, mirroring the existing skip posture for unavailable sinks.

Related host-flake beads: VieNeuTTSApp-b0t, VieNeuTTSApp-o98.

title: [bug] Minor CUDA detection issues: signal ordering, 'CUDA None < 12.8' note, stale [gpu] hint, hardcoded local-runtime pins
description:
Bundle of small issues found reviewing the Windows CUDA detection path:

1. controller.py:_publish_cuda_runtime_driver_probe emits cudaRuntimeDriverChanged (line ~1124) BEFORE assigning _cuda_runtime_driver_version (line ~1128). A synchronous consumer calling managed_cuda_for_detection() during the emit sees (ready=True, version=None) → detect_hardware → cuda_ok=False → 'CUDA None < 12.8' note. Currently masked because the only consumer resolves on a fresh thread, but the ordering is fragile — set the version before emitting.

2. detector.py:probe_torch() never reports cuda_available=True (metadata-only probe), so detect_hardware()'s first branch is dead in production and a working system torch+CUDA (source install) falls to the nvidia_smi branch with cuda_version=None → _describe() emits literal 'CUDA None < 12.8' in the engine note. (Managed-runtime-only is per design spec 2026-09-06 — this is just the cosmetic note.)

3. engine.py ~582: the 'pip install vienetts-app[gpu]' hint is unreachable for backend=torch — the _cuda_runtime is None check raises 'managed CUDA runtime is not installed' before the factory ever runs. Also stale per closed bead VieNeuTTSApp-ce6 ([gpu] installs CPU torch anyway).

4. cuda_runtime.py:_has_compatible_local_torch hardcodes '_C.cp313'/'cpython-313' and version '2.8.0+cu128' instead of deriving from _running_python_tag() and the platform manifest — drift hazard if the interpreter or pinned torch changes. Diagnostic-only, low impact.
close_reason: Fixed all four: driver version assigned before cudaRuntimeDriverChanged is emitted; _describe() no longer prints a literal 'CUDA None'; stale [gpu]/pip hint replaced with managed-runtime guidance; local-runtime discovery derives the Python tag from the interpreter and torch versions from the platform manifest.
